original_question: Let A = direct sum_{i=0}^c A_i be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebra over a field whose characteristic is zero or greater than c, with embedding dimension n. Suppose the symmetric group S_n acts on A by permuting the variables. Must A have the strong Lefschetz property?
target_in_paper: Question 2.7 in Section 2 (the Gorenstein algebras subsection): the paper’s specific open problem about standard graded Artinian Gorenstein algebras with an Sn-action by permuting variables, asking whether they must have the SLP. ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already extremely close to the paper’s official formulation and captures all of its distinctive hypotheses: A = ⊕_{i=0}^c A_i, standard graded Artinian Gorenstein, characteristic 0 or > c, embedding dimension n, an Sn-action by permutation of the variables, and the question whether A has the strong Lefschetz property. This is essentially Question 2.7 almost verbatim. missing_details: To make the question fully stand-alone, identify c explicitly as the socle degree / top nonzero degree of A; the paper encodes this by writing A = ⊕_{i=0}^c A_i. ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf))
Spell out what “embedding dimension n” means, namely n = dim_K(A_1).

Clarify the phrase “Sn acts on A by permuting the variables” by choosing a standard graded presentation A ≅ K[x1, …, xn]/I with I homogeneous and Sn-stable under x_i ↦ x_{σ(i)}; otherwise the word “variables” is not defined for an abstract graded algebra.

Define the strong Lefschetz property explicitly: there exists a linear form ℓ ∈ A_1 such that, for every integer d ≥ 1 and every 0 ≤ i ≤ c − d, the multiplication map ×ℓ^d : A_i → A_{i+d} has maximal rank.
State the universal quantifier plainly: the problem asks whether every algebra satisfying these hypotheses must have the SLP.
refined_question: Let K be a field with char(K) = 0 or char(K) > c, and let A = ⊕_{i=0}^c A_i ≅ K[x1, …, xn]/I be a standard graded Artinian Gorenstein K-algebra of socle degree c and embedding dimension n = dim_K(A_1), where I is homogeneous. Assume that I is stable under the natural action of the symmetric group Sn on K[x1, …, xn] by permuting the variables x1, …, xn, so that Sn acts on A by permutation of the variables. Must A have the strong Lefschetz property; that is, does there exist a linear form ℓ ∈ A_1 such that for every d ≥ 1 and every 0 ≤ i ≤ c − d, the multiplication map ×ℓ^d : A_i → A_{i+d} has maximal rank? ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf))
justification: The draft is targeting Question 2.7 exactly, not the broader neighboring Question 2.6. The telltale extra hypotheses “embedding dimension n” and “the symmetric group Sn acts on A by permutation of the variables” appear in the paper only in Question 2.7, which the authors introduce as a “more specific problem” inside the Gorenstein algebras discussion. The only real sharpening needed is to make explicit the ambient polynomial presentation behind “permutation of the variables” and the definition of the SLP, so that the question is self-contained without changing its scope. The sentence immediately after Question 2.7 further confirms the intended narrow scope by noting that this question is already known in the special case of quadratic complete intersections. ([uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl](https://uniwersalizm.uken.krakow.pl/wp-content/uploads/sites/122/2024/05/Lefschetz-Preparatory-School-Notes-by-Migliore-and-Favacchio-v2-1.pdf))
